query: What is the main mechanism by which large language models generate text?
gold_answer: Large language models generate text by predicting the next token in a sequence using learned probability distributions over a vocabulary conditioned on prior context.
model_answer: LLMs generate text by predicting the next word based on patterns learned during training from large corpora.

query: How does retrieval-augmented generation improve factual accuracy?
gold_answer: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds model outputs in retrieved documents from an external knowledge base reducing hallucinations by providing verifiable source material at inference time.
model_answer: RAG improves accuracy by retrieving relevant documents and conditioning the generator on them so answers are grounded in real sources.
